words: قل هاذه سبيلى أدعوا إلى الله على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعنى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophet travels to God and reaches Him independently, while a saint can travel only by following the Prophet and being guided on his path; each receives stations according to preparedness.
rows.anchor: الفرق بين النبي والولي في ذلك أن النبي مستقل بنفسه في السير إلى الله والوصول ويكون حظه من كل مقام بحسب استعداده الكامل والولي لا يمكنه السير إلا في متابعة النبي

rows.speaker: جنيد البغدادي
rows.claim: Junayd says the Sufi path is constrained by the foundations of the Qur'an and Sunna.
rows.anchor: قال جنيد البغدادي قدس سره مذهبنا هذا مقيد بأصول الكتاب والسنة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says every path is closed to people except the path of following the Messenger's trace.
rows.anchor: قال علي كرم الله وجهه : الطرق كلها مسدودة على الخلق إلا من اقتفى أثر رسول الله

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Al-Sa'di's verse says anyone who opposes the Prophet will never reach the destination; the way of purity is through Mustafa.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ السعدي قدس سره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human weakness means a person cannot endure separation from God for even a moment; humans are praised for this weakness because they are specially marked by mutual love of God.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الإنسان لا يصبر عن الله لحظة لضعفه مهما يكون على الفطرة الإنسانية فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها فإنه يحبهم ويحبونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weakness is both a cause of human perfection and happiness and a cause of deficiency and misery: people shift between animal appetites and angelic praise and obedience.
rows.anchor: هذا الضعف سبب لكمال الإنسان وسعادته وسبب لنقصانه وشقاوته لأنه يتغير لضعفه من حال إلى حال ومن صفة إلى أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only humans possess this capacity to move between animal and angelic qualities; weakness lets them perfect themselves by adopting God's attributes, unlike angels or beasts.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا الاستعداد لغيره حتى الملك لا يقدر أن يتصف بصفات البهيمة والبهيمة لا تقدر أن تتصف بصفة الملك لعدم ضعف الإنسانية

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: A divine hadith promises that whoever obeys God will be made a living king who never dies, illustrating human perfection through obedience.
rows.anchor: أنا ملك حي لا أموت أبدا عبدي أطعني أجعلك ملكا حيا لا يموت أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At perfection a human is the best of creation, while adopting beastly qualities makes him the worst of creation.
rows.anchor: فعند هذا الكمال يكون خير البرية وعند اتصافه بالصفات البهيمية يصير شر البرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book sent in truth is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: {إنآ أنزلنآ إليك الكتاب} أي القرآن إنزالا {بالحق}

words: لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Ansari, Tu'ma b. Ubayriq, stole his neighbor Qatada b. al-Nu'man's armor, hid it with the Jew Zayd b. al-Samin, and flour leaking from its sack led investigators to the Jew.
rows.anchor: روي أن رجلا من الأنصار يقال له طعمة بن أبيرق من بني ظفر سرق درعا من جاره قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tu'ma denied the theft and his people urged the Prophet to prosecute the Jew, relying on their apparent testimony; the Prophet withheld judgment for revelation, which exposed Tu'ma and his witnesses as liars and cleared the Jew.
rows.anchor: فسألوه أن يجادل اليهودي ليدفع فضيحة البهتان عن صاحبهم طعمة وقالوا له عليه السلام أن يعاقب اليهودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Araka means what God made known and revealed to the Prophet; it is not ocular sight or ordinary knowledge, but a recognition called seeing for its force, clarity, and freedom from doubt.
rows.anchor: فأراك ليس من الرؤية البصرية ولا من التي بمعنى العلم وإلا لاستدعى ثلاثة مفاعيل بل هو منقول من رأيت بمعنى الاعتقاد والمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tu'ma's clan knew he had committed the theft, reportedly because he was already a thief in pre-Islamic times, but conspired overnight to blame the Jew and save him from punishment.
rows.anchor: روي أن قومه علموا أن تلك السرقة عمل طعمة بناء على أنه سارق في الجاهلية لكنهم بيتوا طول ليلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traitors are Tu'ma and his helpers; being a disputant for them would mean arguing against the innocent Jew on their behalf.
rows.anchor: أي لأجلهم والذب عنهم وهم طعمة ومن يعينه

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says the Prophet was told to seek forgiveness because he had contemplated a judgment that would have been wrong if carried out, although he was excused before God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ ولما صدر عنه عليه السلام الهم بذلك الحكم الذي لو وقع لكان خطأ في نفسه أمر الله تعالى إياه عليه السلام بأن يستغفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired names emphasize God's abundant forgiveness and mercy toward whoever seeks His forgiveness.
rows.anchor: مبالغا في المغفرة والرحمة لمن يستغفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtiyan and khiyana mean the same; the wrongdoers betray themselves because the harm of their sin returns to them, as in saying that someone who wrongs another has wronged only himself.
rows.anchor: الاختيان والخيانة بمعنى أي يخونونها بالمعصية وإنما قال يختانون أنفسهم وإن كانوا ما خانوا أنفسهم لأن مضرة خيانتهم راجعة إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people described as betraying themselves may be Tu'ma and those like him.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالموصول إما طعمة وأمثاله وإما هو ومن عاونه وشهد ببراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the reference includes Tu'ma's helpers and the clan members who testified to his innocence, since they share his sin.
rows.anchor: إما هو ومن عاونه وشهد ببراءته من قومه فإنهم شركاء له في الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that God does not love someone is a metonym for His hatred and displeasure.
rows.anchor: عدم المحبة كناية عن البغض والسخط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwan denotes excessive, persistent betrayal and athim someone engrossed in sin; the intensive forms describe Tu'ma despite one theft because his wicked nature inclined him to repeat both acts.
rows.anchor: {من كان خوانا} مفرطا في الخيانة مصرا عليها {أثيما} منهمكا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tu'ma reportedly fled to Mecca, apostatized, and later died when a wall collapsed on him as he tried to steal household goods.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أنه هرب إلى مكة وارتد ونقب حائطا بها ليسرق متاع أهله فسقط الحائط عليه فقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A maxim warns that a discovered sin is likely to have further sins associated with it.
rows.anchor: قيل إذا عثرت من رجل على سيئة فاعلم أن لها أخوات

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: When a thief's mother pleaded that this was his first theft, Umar replied that she lied, since God does not punish a servant for the first time.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه أمر بقطع يد سارق فجاءت أمه تبكي وتقول هذه أول سرقة سرقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They conceal themselves from people out of shame and fear of harm, but cannot conceal themselves from God.
rows.anchor: {يستخفون من الناس} يستترون منهم حياء وخوفا من ضررهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor and mercy here mean protection: a party of Banu Zafar defending Tu'ma intended to mislead the Prophet from a just judgment by disguising the facts.
rows.anchor: {ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته} بالعصمة {لهمت طآئفة منهم} أي من بني ظفر وهم الذابون عن طعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording does not deny that they intended to mislead the Prophet; it denies that their effort had any effect on him.
rows.anchor: وليس القصد فيه إلى نفي همهم بل إلى نفي تأثيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their misguidance harms only themselves because its consequence falls back on them.
rows.anchor: {وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم} لأن وبالهم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot harm the Prophet at all because God protects him; his passing thought relied on outward appearances and was not bias in judgment.
rows.anchor: {وما يضرونك من شىء} محل الجار والمجرور النصب على المصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Qur'an, and the wisdom is its legal rulings, through which God taught what is lawful and unlawful.
rows.anchor: {وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب} أي القرآن {والحكمة} أي ما في القرآن من الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught the Prophet unseen and hidden matters through revelation, things he had not known before that teaching.
rows.anchor: {وعلمك} بالوحي من الغيب وخفيات الأمور {ما لم تكن تعلم} ذلك إلى وقت التعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great favor includes universal prophethood and complete leadership, along with God's protection and teaching.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك الفضل العظيم عصمته وتعليمه ما لم يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports al-Haddadi's ruling that nobody may advocate for another to establish or deny a right without knowing the facts.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآيات دلالة أنه لا يجوز لأحد أن يخاصم لغيره في إثبات حق أو نفيه غير عالم بحقيقة أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports al-Haddadi's rule that a judge may not favor one litigant over another, even when one is Muslim and the other a non-Muslim.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يجوز للحاكم الميل إلى أحد الخصمين وإن كان أحدهما مسلما والآخر كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports al-Haddadi's ruling that possession of stolen property alone does not require judgment that its holder stole it.
rows.anchor: وأن وجود السرقة في يدي إنسان لا يوجب الحكم بها عليه

rows.speaker: الصائب
rows.claim: The author says evil's consequence returns to its perpetrator, just as good benefits its doer; al-Sa'ib's poem illustrates that the oppressor first suffers the effect of his injustice.
rows.anchor: قال الصائب : أول بظالمان أثر ظلم ميرسد يش از هدف هميشه كمان ناله ميكند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tale says God dried the hand of a man slaughtering a calf before its mother, then restored it when a bird's chick returned from its nest to its mother; the saying warns against selling people, cutting trees, or slaughtering cattle.
rows.anchor: حكي أن الله تعالى أيبس يد رجل يذبح عجل بقرة بين يدي أمه ثم ردها برد فرخ سقط من وكره إلى أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman gave a morsel to a beggar; later a wolf took her child, and God returned the child unharmed, explaining that the rescue answered the morsel she had given.
rows.anchor: حكي أن امرأة وضعت لقمة في فم سائل ثم ذهبت إلى مزرعة فوضعت ولدها في موضع فأخذه الذئب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge and wisdom are among the greatest virtues, especially beneficial knowledge that brings a person nearer to God; the Prophet's prayer seeks refuge from knowledge that does not benefit.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن العلم والحكمة من أعظم الفضائل والمراد العلم النافع المقرب إلى الله تعالى أعاذنا الله مما لم ينفع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the Prophet's prayer for refuge from knowledge that brings no benefit.
rows.anchor: في دعائه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Muslim transmits from Abu Hurayra that a person's deeds cease at death except for ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who prays for them.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant should attribute every virtue to God's favor and mercy rather than praise the self; self-admiration dims inward lights of certainty, and even a lifetime of deeds cannot repay the gift of existence.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن لا يرى العبد الفضائل والخيرات من نفسه بل من فضل الله ورحمته وليس للعبد أن يزكي نفسه

rows.speaker: شاه شعاع الكرماني
rows.claim: Shah Shuja al-Kirmani offered to trade fifty years of pilgrimage for a single good deed given to a poor man; when a jurist accused him of slighting the law, he said he saw no value in himself or his deeds.
rows.anchor: حكي عن شاه شعاع الكرماني أنه كان جالسا في مسجد فقام فقير وسأل الناس فلم يعطوه شيئا فقال الكرماني من يشتري حج خمسين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility about deeds does not mean abandoning work: people should perform every good act without valuing it, seeing their ability and success as God's enabling grace.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد التعطيل عن العمل بل يعملون جميع الحسنات ولا يرون لها قدرا بل يرون التوفيق لها من فضل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Al-Sa'di's verse says any good that reaches another person comes through God's enabling grace, so the servant should praise God and not regard himself.
rows.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine favor is a gift from God, not something a servant can earn or attract; it guides a servant to faith and enables righteous action.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في الآية أن فضل الله موهبة من مواهب الحق يؤتيه من يشاء وليس لأحد فيه مدخل بالكسب والاستجلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author interprets the great favor as God Himself, who is the Prophet's favor and mercy to the worlds, and cites the saying that the heavens were created for him.
rows.anchor: والعظيم في قوله : {وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما} هو الله تعالى أي أن الله العظيم هو فضل الله عليك ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the saying, 'Were it not for you, I would not have created the spheres,' as a report of the Prophet's immense favor.
rows.anchor: كما أنك فضل الله ورحمته على العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Part of God's favor was that nothing spiritual or bodily diverted the Prophet from the path of arrival; the author prays for protection from outward and inward obstacles and union with holy souls.
rows.anchor: ومن فضل الله عليك أنه لم يضله شيء من الروحانيات والجسمانيات عن طريق الوصول اللهم احفظنا من الموانع في طريق الوصول إليك آفاقية أو أنفسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joshua asked Moses in a dream how death felt; Moses likened it to being skinned alive. Moses lived 120 years, and after his death and forty years God sent Joshua as prophet to fight the giants.
rows.anchor: وكان عمر موسى مائة وعشرين سنة فلما مات موسى وانقضت الأربعون بعث الله يوشع نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joshua led the Israelites to Jericho with the Ark; after six months' siege they sounded horns and shouted together, the wall fell, and they defeated the giants.
rows.anchor: معه تابوت الميثاق فأحاط بمدينة أريحاء ستة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When sunset approached on Friday and the Sabbath was near, Joshua prayed for more daylight; the sun stopped and the day was lengthened so he could finish the battle, after which he conquered thirty-one Syrian kings and all Syria.
rows.anchor: وكان القتال يوم الجمعة فبقيت منهم البقية وكادت الشمس تغرب وتدخل ليلة السبت فقال : اللهم اردد الشمس علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collected spoils did not burn until a thief was identified by an allegiance test; he produced a jeweled golden bull's head, which was placed in the offering, and fire consumed both it and him.
rows.anchor: وجمع الغنائم فلم تنزل النار فأوحى الله إلى يوشع أن فيها غلولا فمرهم فليبايعوك فبايعوه فالتصقت يد رجل منهم بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Joshua was buried on Mount Ephraim at age 126 after directing Israel for twenty-seven years.
rows.anchor: ثم مات يوشع ودفن في جبل افرائيم وكان عمره مائة وستا وعشرين سنة وتدبيره أمر بني إسرائيل بعد موت موسى سبعا وعشرين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet accompanying the account says the world will remain with no one, so the heart should attach only to the Creator of the world.
rows.anchor: جهان أي بردار نماند بكس دل اندر جهان آفرين بندوبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to recite to the People of Scripture the true and accurate account of Adam's two sons, Cain and Abel.
rows.anchor: {نبأ ابنى ءادم} أي : خبر ابني أبي البشر وهما قابيل وهابيل

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars say Eve bore twins, boy and girl, in each pregnancy except Seth's; Adam was told to marry each son to the other's twin because there were no other women.
rows.anchor: ذكر العلماء أن حواء كانت تلد في كل بطن ولدين ذكرا وأنثى الاشيثا فإنها ولدته منفردا فولدت أول بطن قابيل وأخته اقليما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain's twin was more beautiful, so he envied Abel, resented what he thought was Adam's decision, and demanded that both offer sacrifices, with the accepted offering deciding who married her.
rows.anchor: وكانت توأمة قابيل أجمل فحسد عليها أخاه وسخط وزعم أن ذلك ليس من عند الله بل من جهة آدم فقال لهما قربا قربانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurban means something by which one seeks nearness to God, such as an animal sacrifice or charity; it is singular because it began as a verbal noun, with each brother bringing one understood.
rows.anchor: والقربان اسم لما يتقرب به إلى الله تعالى من ذبيحة أو صدقة وتوحيده لما أنه في الأصل مصدر والتقدير إذ قرب كل منهما قربانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel, who raised livestock, brought a fine camel or ram with milk and butter; after Adam prayed, a smokeless white fire descended from heaven and consumed it.
rows.anchor: هو هابيل وكان صاحب ضرع وقرب جملا سمينا أو كبشا ولبنا وزبدا فنزلت نار من السماء بيضاء لا دخان لها فأكلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that era, a heavenly fire consuming an offering marked its acceptance; when an offering was not accepted, the fire did not descend and birds or beasts ate it. Another explanation is that there were then no poor recipients for charity.
rows.anchor: وكانت القرابين إذا كانت مقبولة نزلت من السماء نار فأكلتها وإن لم تكن مقبولة لم تنزل النار وأكلتها الطير والسباع

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr and others report that fire from heaven carried Abel's offering up to Paradise, where it remained until it was used to ransom the one sacrificed.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير وغيره نزلت نار من السماء فاحتملت قربان هابيل ورفع بها إلى الجنة فلم يزل يرعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain farmed crops and offered the worst wheat; fire did not touch it because he resented God's judgment, lacked sincere intent, and deliberately offered his poorest produce.
rows.anchor: وهو قابيل كان صاحب زرع وقرب اردأ ما عنده من القمح ولم تتعرض له النار أصلا لأنه سخط حكم الله ولم يخلص النية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the rejected offering, Cain's jealousy grew while Adam was away in Mecca; he threatened Abel because God had accepted Abel's sacrifice, Abel would marry the beautiful sister, and Abel's descendants might boast over his.
rows.anchor: وقد غضب قابيل لرد قربانه وكان يضمر الحسد في نفسه إلى أن أتى آدم مكة لزيارة البيت فلما غاب آدم أتيى قابيل هابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain's stated reasons for murder were that God accepted Abel's sacrifice, Abel would marry the prettier sister, and people would say Abel was better and his descendants would boast over Cain.
rows.anchor: قال : ولم قال لأن الله قبل قربانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel says God accepts offerings only from the God-fearing; the different outcomes reflect their piety, so Cain's failure comes from himself, not Abel.
rows.anchor: {إنما يتقبل الله} أي : القربان {من المتقين} لا من غيرهم وإنما تقبل قرباني ورد قربانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the Prophet's gesture to his heart as an explanation of where piety resides.
rows.anchor: والتقوى من صفات القلب لقوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True piety means acting with fear that one's worship is deficient, carefully avoiding worship for any purpose besides God's pleasure, and excluding any partner from it.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة التقوى أن يكون العامل على خوف ووجل من تقصير نفسه فيما أتى به من الطاعات وأن يكون في غاية الاحتراز من أن يأتي بتلك الطاعة لغرض سوى طلب مرضاة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel says that even if Cain reaches out to kill him, Abel will not do the same in return.
rows.anchor: ما أنا بفاعل مثله لك في وقت من الأوقات ثم علل ذلك بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Abel was physically stronger but refrained from killing his brother and submitted out of fear of God because defensive killing was not permitted then.
rows.anchor: قيل كان هابيل أقوى ولكن تحرج عن قتله واستسلم له خوفا من الله تعالى لأن القتل للدفع لم يكن مباحا في ذلك الوقت

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says Islamic law allows a person targeted for killing to submit and yield in hope of reward, as Uthman did.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : وفي الشرع جائز لمن أريد قتله أن ينقاد ويستسلم طلبا للأجر كما فعل عثمان رضي الله عنه

words: إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓأَ بِإِثْمِى وَإِثْمِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel gives a further, independently sufficient reason for not retaliating: he wants to remain free of sin while Cain bears his own sin and the equivalent of the victim's sin caused by the aggression.
rows.anchor: تعليل آخر لامتناعه عن المعارضة على أنه غرض متأخر عنه كما أن الأول باعث متقدم عليه وإنما لم يعطف تنبيها على كفاية كل منهما في العلية

words: إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓأَ بِإِثْمِى وَإِثْمِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites a Prophetic report that when two people trade insults, the initiator bears both people's sin unless the wronged person exceeds the bounds.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points to becoming one of the people of the Fire; this is the punishment of someone who is not content with God's judgment.
rows.anchor: {وذالك} إشارة إلى كونه من أصحاب النار {إنى أريد} أي : عقوبة من لم يرض بحكم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb comes from the expression for pasture becoming spacious: Cain's soul made killing his brother seem easy, open, and unconfined.
rows.anchor: {فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه} من طاع له المرتع إذا اتسع أي : وسعته وسهلته أي جعلته سهلا وهونته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlawful murder, especially of a brother, should appear wholly repugnant to reason and religious law; the commanding soul makes it easy by deploying its predatory, angry force.
rows.anchor: فإن قتل النفس بغير حق لا سيما قتل الأخ إذا تصوره الإنسان يجده شيئا عاصيا نافرا كل النفرة عن دائرة الشرع والعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording depicts the soul as making the act compliant to it, like a rebel made obedient; the added laam strengthens the connection though the sentence works without it.
rows.anchor: فكأن النفس صيرته كالمطيع لها بعد أن كان كالعاصي المتمرد عليها ويتم الكلام بدون اللام بأن يقال فطوعته نفسه قتل أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The laam is an added connective; the clause is complete without it, just as one could say 'I preserved Zayd's property' without the laam construction.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه جيىء باللام لزيادة الربط كما في قولك حفظت لزيد ماله مع تمام الكلام بأن يقال حفظت مال زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Cain did not know how to kill; the Devil demonstrated by smashing a bird or snake's head against a stone, and Cain copied him while Abel submitted. Another says Cain ambushed Abel in his sleep.
rows.anchor: قيل لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتل هابيل فتمثل إبليس وأخذ طائرا أو حية وضع رأسه على الحجر ثم شدخها بحجر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account places the killing near Mount Thawr, the pass of Hira, or Basra at the site of its great mosque, and says Abel was twenty years old.
rows.anchor: وهو مستسلم لا يستعصي عليه أو اغتاله وهو نائم وغنمه ترعى وذلك عند جبل ثور أو عقبة حراء أو بالبصرة في موضع المسجد الأعظم وكان لهابيل يوم قتله عشرون سنة

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: A report from one of the great masters says Adam vomited what he had eaten on descending to earth; a poisonous tree grew from it, the snake ate the poison and became deadly, and Cain was conceived from what remained and became a murderer and corrupter.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض الكبار أن آدم لما هبط إلى الأرض تفكر فيما أكل فاستقاء فنبتت شجرة السم من قيئه فأكلت الحية ذلك السم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain lost both his religion and his worldly life.
rows.anchor: {فأصبح من الخاسرين} خسر دينه ودنياه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Cain lost this world by angering his parents and remaining condemned until the Resurrection, and lost the next world through great punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : خسر دنياه وآخرته أما الدنيا فإنه أسخط لوالديه وبقي مذموما إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raven was sent, and yahthathu means to dig; li-yuriyahu may have God or the raven as its implicit subject, with different possible attachments for the laam.
rows.anchor: يبحث فى الأرض} البحث بالفارسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuwari means conceal; his brother's saw'a is the corpse, which is shameful to leave visible, or specifically his nakedness because his clothes had been taken.
rows.anchor: {كيف يوارى} يستر {سوءة أخيه} أي جسده الميت فإنه مما يستقبح أنه يرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayfa describes the implicit object of yuwari, and the clause is the second object of yara.
rows.anchor: وكيف حال من ضمير يواري والجملة ثاني مفعولي يرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain left the first human corpse in open country and did not know what to do; he carried it in a sack for forty days or a year until it decayed as beasts and birds watched.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما قتله تركه بالعراء أي الأرض الخالية عن الأشجار ولم يدر ما يصنع به لأنه كان أول ميت على وجه الأرض من بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent two ravens that fought; one killed the other, dug a grave with its beak and feet, and buried it while Cain watched.
rows.anchor: فبعث الله غرابين فاقتتلا فقتل أحدهما الآخر فحفر له فمنقاره ورجليه حفرة فألقاه فيها وواراه وقابيل ينظر إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ya waylata is an anguished cry of regret; the alif replaces the speaker's ya, and it means 'my ruin, come, for now is your time.'
rows.anchor: هي كلمة جزع وتحسر والألف بدل من ياء المتكلم والمعنى يا ويلتي احضري فهذا أوانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling something inanimate is a figurative way to express grief, as in the Qur'anic phrase 'O regret upon the servants'; wayl and wayla mean destruction.
rows.anchor: والنداء وإن كان أصله لمن يتأتى منه الإقبال وهم العقلاء إلا أن العرب تتجوز وتنادي ما لا يعقل إظهارا للتحسر ومثله يا حسرة على العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means, 'Was I unable to be like this raven and bury my brother's body?' It voices astonishment that Cain failed to learn what the raven showed him.
rows.anchor: تعجب من عدم اهتدائه إلى ما اهتدى إليه الغراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb fa-uwari is in the subjunctive, coordinated with akuna: unable to be like the raven and thereby burying the body.
rows.anchor: وقوله : فأواري بالنصب عطف على أكون أي أعجزت عن كوني مشبها بالغراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain regretted his confusion, carrying the corpse, and related trouble, not his sin from fear of God; this regret was not repentance and did not benefit him.
rows.anchor: فلما كان ندمه لأجل هذه الأسباب لا للخوف من الله بسبب ارتكاب المعصية لم يكن ندمه توبة ولم ينتفع بندمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, Cain's soul represents the lower self and his brother represents the heart; the self, the heart's greatest enemy, made killing it seem permissible.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في قوله : {فطوعت له نفسه} أي : نفس قابيل النفس طوعت له وجوزت {قتل أخيه} وهو القلب لأن النفس أعدى عدو القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Killing the heart makes the self lose in both worlds: here it forfeits spiritual arrivals, unveilings, unseen knowledge, witnessing, and intimacy, becoming ignorant and lost; the author links this to the short sura al-Asr.
rows.anchor: في قتل القلب خسارة النفس في الدنيا والآخرة أما في الدنيا فتحرم عن الواردات والكشوف والعلوم الغيبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the next world, killing the heart costs the self entry to the gardens, vision of the Generous Lord, and rescue from Hell and painful punishment.
rows.anchor: وأما في الآخرة فتخسر الدخول في جنات النعيم ولقاء الرب الكريم والنجاة من الجحيم والعذاب الأليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can teach people through any creature, including a raven, just as He teaches prophets through angels and communities through prophets.
rows.anchor: {فبعث الله} إشارات منها ليعلم أن الله قادر على أن يبعث {غرابا} أو غيره من الحيوان إلى الإنسان ليعلمه ما لم يعلم كما يبعث الملائكة إلى الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaching through a raven reminds angels and prophets not to take pride in being specially taught, since God teaches through them as well as through animals.
rows.anchor: ومنها لئلا يعجب الملائكة والرسل أنفسهم باختصاصهم بتعليم الحق فإنه يعلمهم بواسطة الغراب كما يعلمهم بواسطة الملائكة والرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story shows that a human may need a raven as a teacher and may fail to equal a raven in knowledge.
rows.anchor: ومنها ليعلم الإنسان أنه محتاج في التعلم إلى غراب ويعجز أن يكون مثل غراب في العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every animal, indeed every atom, is a sign of God's oneness and free choice, since intelligible behavior appears in creatures without reason.
rows.anchor: في كل حيوان بل في كل ذرة آية تدل على وحدانيته واختياره حيث يبدي المعاملات المعقولة من الحيوانات الغير العاقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading sees God's kindness in providing livelihood and guiding people through subtle means when they face a difficulty.
rows.anchor: ومنها إظهار لطفه مع عباده في أسباب التعيش حتى إذا أشكل عليهم أمر كيف يرشدهم إلى الاحتيال بلطائف الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase begins the intended lesson of the Adam story: it introduces further crimes of the Children of Israel and links them to the gravity and ugliness of unjust killing.
rows.anchor: {من أجل ذالك} شروع فيما هو المقصود بتلاوة النبأ من بيان بعض آخر من جنايات بني إسرائيل ومعاصيهم وذلك إشارة إلى عظم شأن القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unjust killing contains loss of religious and worldly virtues and afterlife happiness, and brings irreparable trial and regret; these harms summarize the earlier descriptions of Cain as loser and regretful.
rows.anchor: أي من أجل كون القتل على سبيل العدوان مشتملا على أنواع المفاسد من خسارة جميع الفضائل الدينية والدنيوية وجمع السعادات الأخروية كما هي مندرجة في إجمال قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajl originally names the verbal noun for committing or provoking evil, then broadened to mean cause; min marks the starting point and is linked to God's clause.
rows.anchor: وأجل في الأصل مصدر أجل شرا إذا جناه وهيجه استعمل في تعليل الجنايات أي في جعل ما جناه الغير علة لأمر يقال فعلته من أجلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet before the explanation advises accepting what has been given and laying aside a frown, since neither party was granted choice.
rows.anchor: رضا بداده بده وزجبين كره بكشاي كه بر من وتوردر اختيار نكشادست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prays to be among those granted divine care, special enabling, and guidance.
rows.anchor: اللهم اجعلنا ممن سبقت له العناية وتقدم في حقه التوفيق الخاص والهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not take Jews and Christians as allies; they are allies of one another, while your allies are God, His Messenger, and the believers, so grant loyalty to them alone.
rows.anchor: أي لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء لأن بعضهم أولياء بعض وليسوا بأوليائكم إنما أولياؤكم الله ورسوله والمؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Citing al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya, the author says loyalty to God means opposing everything besides Him, as Abraham says they are enemies except the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: فموالاة الله في معاداة ما سوى الله كما قال الخليل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Citing al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya, the author explains that loyalty to the Messenger requires opposing the self and resisting desire; a cited saying says desire must follow what the Prophet brought.
rows.anchor: وموالاة الرسول في معاداة النفس ومخالفة الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites a Prophetic saying that faith is incomplete until the Messenger is more beloved than a person's self, wealth, children, and all people.
rows.anchor: لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى أكون أحب إليه من نفسه وماله وولده والناس أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Citing al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya, the author says loyalty to believers means fraternity in religion; the Qur'an calls believers brothers and a Prophetic saying enjoins loving for one's brother what one loves for oneself.
rows.anchor: وموالاة المؤمنين في مؤاخاتهم في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase alladhina is appositional to alladhina amanu.
rows.anchor: {إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين} بدل من الذين آمنوا {وهم راكعون} حال من فاعل الفعلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause wa-hum raki'un is circumstantial for the agents of both verbs, and ruku is explained as humility and lowliness.
rows.anchor: {وهم راكعون} حال من فاعل الفعلين أي يعملون ما ذكر من إقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وهم خاشعون ومتواضعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is to distinguish sincere believers from hypocrites: sincerity appears through regular prayer and almsgiving in a state of humble submission.
rows.anchor: والمقصود تمييز المؤمن المخلص ممن يدعي الإيمان ويكون منافقا لأن الإخلاص إنما يعرف بكونه مواظبا على الصلاة والزكاة في حال الركوع أي في حال الخشوع والإخبات

words: وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever takes God, the Messenger, and believers as allies will be victorious.
rows.anchor: {ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين ءامنوا} أي ومن يتخذهم أولياء {فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit phrase God's party replaces a pronoun to prove the outcome: those who ally with these figures are God's party and therefore victorious; it honors them and implies other allies belong to Satan's party.
rows.anchor: ولكن وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر تنبيها على البرهان عليه وكأنه قيل ومن يتول هؤلاء فهم حزب الله وحزب الله هم الغالبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hizb means a person's companions or supporters, and also a group gathered for a shared cause.
rows.anchor: وحزب الرجل أصحابه والحزب الطائفة يجتمعون لأمر حزبهم أي أصابهم
